Transcript:
[00:00:05] Maya Chen: alright everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood, i lead the onboarding for enterprise customers, um we'll run through the staging playbook, the network layout, and then capture open action items, sound good?
[00:00:18] Priya Rao: yep, thanks Maya, excited to get this moving. quick note - our pilot target is production-like traffic but limited to internal users, so latency target is 150 to 200ms p95 for short prompts, and throughput around 60 rps at peak, just to set context.
[00:00:34] Liam O'Neill: okay good, that helps. so we're thinking Redwood Dedicated for the pilot or are you planning to try Private? curious on constraints.
[00:00:46] Daniel Kim: we prefer Private in our VPC eventually but for staging we want a hybrid approach — public infra for smoke tests then move to private. also need to confirm peering and firewall rules.
[00:00:59] Jared Patel: that aligns with a lot we do; we can support hybrid. the playbook we'll share shows both flows.
[00:01:12] Sofia Alvarez: from security, we need K M S integration, audit logs shipped to our SIEM and S S O mapped to groups so only product can call certain routes. also encryption at rest plus key import restrictions — is that supported?
[00:01:26] Liam O'Neill: yes on K M S we support customer-managed keys in Private and we can integrate with common K M S providers, there's a couple of notes though on import policies and rotation schedule, we'll share the exact constraints. sometimes the terminology in our docs comes out as 'K M S' spelled, sorry the auto-transcript does odd spacing.
[00:01:43] Tom Baker: can you give a quick overview of the staging topology? where do requests land and how does traffic get routed?
[00:01:51] Maya Chen: sure, high-level: for staging you have two options: 1) Redwood Hosted with VPC egress and proxying to your VPC for data-plane interactions, or 2) Redwood Private which runs the control plane in our managed environment and inference nodes in your V P C/on-prem. for the hybrid flow we'd front the calls through a small hosted ingress that can route into Private nodes once peering is established. Liam do you want the diagram?
[00:02:14] Liam O'Neill: yeah let me share the diagram — (link posted in chat) — points to note: the KV cache will be colocated with the inference pool, we do prefix caching when prompts match, and batcher settings will need tuning for your short prompt distribution to keep latencies low.
[00:02:31] Priya Rao: kv cache? you mean K V? okay, got it. question — what's the default batch size behavior and how does that affect p95?
[00:02:40] Liam O'Neill: default is adaptive; it grows with concurrency. for short prompts it usually stays small but we can pin batching and set max latency to maintain p95. in practice for 150ms target we recommend continuous batching off or low batch window and a N best-1 fallback for bigger requests.
[00:02:58] Aisha Mensah: from SRE side i'm concerned about burst spikes and autoscaling. do you expose metrics and can we set SLO alerts?
[00:03:07] Jared Patel: yes we have per-route latency and token breakdowns in Console. you can configure alerts and there's an API to pull traces. we'll also provide a sample grafana dashboard for the pilot.
[00:03:21] Daniel Kim: network specifics — what CIDR do you expect for peering and do we need NAT? also are there specific ports for the inference nodes?
[00:03:30] Liam O'Neill: typical peering is /16 or /20 depending on scale; we'll include the exact ranges in the runbook. inference nodes talk over TLS on port 443 for control and a few internal ports for metrics, but all traffic can be routed over the peered interface, no public ingress required.
[00:03:45] Sofia Alvarez: and for audit logs — are they pushed to our S I E M or do we pull from Redwood? we want immutable logs for compliance.
[00:03:53] Maya Chen: two options — push or pull. for Private we can forward to your SIEM via a secure syslog or Kinesis connector; for Hosted we'll give you log exports and signed audit packages for the window.
[00:04:07] Tom Baker: earlier you mentioned fallbacks to hosted models if Dedicated is saturated, how seamless is that? we worry about behavior differences.
[00:04:16] Liam O'Neill: good point. we can configure model-variant routing rules — e.g., if latency exceeds threshold or capacity hit then route to a compatible hosted variant. we tag variants and track quality differences in the Console. you'll see a flag when fallback happened and can auto-rollback or notify. note: there can be small quality deltas, we'll surface evals so you can approve.
[00:04:37] Priya Rao: evals are crucial — we need a way to link prompt families to regression alerts. is that part of Redwood Optimize?
[00:04:44] Jared Patel: yes Redwood Optimize ties prompt sets to quality monitors and can send regression alerts if output drift occurs after a model change. we'll onboard your canonical prompt suite as part of the pilot.
[00:05:00] Maya Chen: quick logistics: we'll send the staging runbook with network CIDRs, SSO mapping template, and a checklist for K M S. Priya, can you confirm the pilot window — you mentioned next month?
[00:05:12] Priya Rao: target start is Oct 12th for a two-week smoke phase, then expand. timeline depends on peering and SSO mapping.
[00:05:21] Aisha Mensah: can we have a canary first with 10 internal users for 48 hours? get basic metrics then scale to 60 rps.
[00:05:26] Maya Chen: absolutely that's our recommended approach.
[00:05:30] [00:30:10] Liam O'Neill: (later in meeting) on quantization — if you intend to use 8-bit quantized models we recommend testing end-to-end because latency profiles shift; sometimes 8-bit helps throughput but adds a small decode penalty for short sequences. i'll put together a short doc with tradeoffs.
[00:30:45] Daniel Kim: regarding cost, can we get an estimate for token consumption for our prompt families? we have some long system prompts and chain-of-thought traces.
[00:31:00] Jared Patel: yes we'll ask you to upload sample prompts and traffic mix; we have a token estimator sheet that simulates per-day cost at different batching configs. we'll share that sheet after the call.
[00:31:18] Sofia Alvarez: one more on compliance — we need evidence of SOC2 in the onboarding binder and a brief of data residency controls.
[00:31:27] Maya Chen: we have a SOC2 package and a security playbook, we'll share both in gated S3 link. also note: for Private deployments we can localize logs and storage to your region.
[00:31:40] Tom Baker: workflow question — who will drive day-to-day ops during the pilot? we prefer a single point of contact.
[00:31:47] Priya Rao: Priya will be point for product and we'll designate Daniel for infra/peering; Sofia for security sign-off.
[00:31:55] Maya Chen: great, we'll record that in the runbook.
[00:32:05] [00:45:22] Jared Patel: recap and next steps — action items we'll enumerate: Maya will send runbook + network diagram by 9/15; Daniel to confirm peering CIDRs and firewall 9/17; Sofia to share SOC2 scoping and K M S requirements 9/16; Liam will produce quantization and latency recommendations 9/20; schedule infra walkthrough week of 9/20.
[00:45:48] Priya Rao: sounds good. can we also get an onboarding checklist for the product team so they know which routes and API keys to use?
[00:45:57] Liam O'Neill: yes a minimal checklist for product and SDK snippets will be included.
[00:46:05] Aisha Mensah: last item — can we enable synthetic traffic generator for the smoke test so we can run load without real users?
[00:46:13] Jared Patel: yes we'll provide a generator and scripts.
[00:46:20] Maya Chen: perfect. any other questions?
[00:46:24] Tom Baker: not from product.
[00:46:27] Priya Rao: no, all good.
[00:46:30] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the runbook and links in the next 48 hours and book the infra walkthrough. appreciate your time.
[00:46:41] [00:57:59] Meeting ended
